# jszip (vendored)

The UMD build of [`jszip`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/jszip), copied here
because this front-end has no bundler and no npm build step. Dual MIT/GPLv3
licensed; see LICENSE.

`jszip.min.mjs` and `jszip.esm.mjs` are not vendored/named as `.js`
deliberately: Node picks a plain `.js` file's module system from the
nearest package.json (this repo doesn't declare `"type": "module"`), which
would make `jszip.min.mjs`'s UMD wrapper load as CommonJS under Node
(`module.exports = ...`) instead of assigning the global the shim reads.
`.mjs` is unconditionally ESM, in the browser and under Node alike, so both
take the UMD wrapper's "assign to the global" branch.

`jszip.esm.mjs` is not part of the npm package: it is a tiny ES module
shim, generated by the vendoring script, that imports `jszip.min.mjs` for
its side effect and re-exports the global (`globalThis.JSZip`) as the
default export. It exists because pptxgenjs's ES module build imports
`jszip` by bare specifier, which Node resolves against `node_modules` but
the browser rejects outright (issue #977 / kevinmcaleer/Snakie#977) — see
`../pptxgenjs/pptxgen.es.js`, which `scripts/vendor-pptxgenjs.mjs` rewrites
to import this shim by relative path instead.

`VERSION` records the release in this directory. It is pinned in the root
`package.json` and copied by a script; never edit these files by hand.

To move to a new release:

```bash
# in the repository root
npm install --save-dev --save-exact jszip@<version>
npm run vendor:jszip
npm run vendor:pptxgenjs   # re-applies the import rewrite against the fresh copy
```

`tests/test_pptx_browser_export.mjs` fails if `VERSION` does not match the
pinned release, or if the files here differ from the installed package.

Used indirectly by `static/pptx-export.js`, which builds PowerPoint decks
in the browser (issue #791), via the vendored `pptxgenjs` in `../pptxgenjs`.
